pinacosaurus-hilwitnorum:study:1.title: The morphology and systematics of Pinacosaurus (Historical Biology, 2026)

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: The type locality of Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum is the Djadochta Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Type locality: Djadochta Formation

facts.statement: Fully grown Pinacosaurus individuals reached about 5 m in total length.
facts.quote: fully grown individuals reached a total length of 5 m.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the body mass of Pinacosaurus at 1.9 tonnes.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated its body mass at 1.9 t

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz estimated Pinacosaurus’s mass to be comparable to that of a horse.
facts.quote: while Thomas R. Holtz estimated it to have a body mass of a horse

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus’s upper snout armor consists of a fused mass rather than separate caputegulae tiles.
facts.quote: The upper snout armour does not consist of distinct tiles, caputegulae, but of a fused mass.

facts.statement: Adult Pinacosaurus skulls are longer than they are wide.
facts.quote: Adult individuals have a skull that is longer than wide.

facts.statement: P. grangeri has a notch in the snout armor just above the innermost nostril opening.
facts.quote: P. grangeri has a notch in the snout armour just above the innermost nostril opening.

facts.statement: P. mephistocephalus possesses squamosal horns that extend beyond the rear of the skull roof, with their points marking the widest part of the skull.
facts.quote: P. mephistocephalus has squamosal horns extending to behind beyond the rear of the skull roof, their points representing the widest point of the skull

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus’s praemaxillae were exceptionally smooth and in life were covered by a horn sheet forming the upper beak.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus has exceptionally smooth praemaxillae, front snout bones, forming the bone core of the upper beak, that was in life covered with a horn sheet.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Pinacosaurus bears roughly fourteen teeth.
facts.quote: The maxilla bears about fourteen teeth.

facts.statement: Juvenile Pinacosaurus specimens preserve large paraglossalia that show signs of muscular stress, indicating a common ankylosaur feature of a muscular tongue.
facts.quote: A juvenile specimen of Pinacosaurus preserves large paraglossalia (triangular bones or cartilages located in the tongue) which show signs of muscular stress

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus likely relied heavily on a muscular tongue and hyobranchia for feeding because its teeth were small and replaced slowly.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus and other ankylosaurs likely relied heavily on muscular tongues and hyobranchia (tongue bones) when feeding, since their teeth were fairly small and were replaced at a relatively slow rate

facts.statement: Its diet may have included tough leaves and pulpy fruits and possibly insects, suggesting a varied or even ant‑eater‑like feeding behavior.
facts.quote: they may have had a more varied diet, including tough leaves and pulpy fruits. Inversely, this might suggest ant-eater-like insectivorous behaviour

facts.statement: Juvenile Pinacosaurus individuals found together at Bayan Mandahu were all oriented the same way, interpreted as a travelling herd killed by a sandstorm.
facts.quote: the individuals were all oriented into the same direction, suggesting they represent a travelling true herd simultaneously killed and covered by a sandstorm

facts.statement: In juvenile Pinacosaurus, ribs fused with vertebrae early in development, and the forelimbs became much more robust than the hindlimbs, indicating the arms bore most of the weight.
facts.quote: During their ontogenetic development, in juveniles at first the ribs fused with their vertebrae. The forelimbs strongly increased in robustness, while the hindlimbs did not become larger relative to the rest of the skeleton, indicating that the arms bore most of the weight

facts.statement: Cervical halfrings in juveniles developed bony outgrowths that connected with underlying osteoderms, which then fused together.
facts.quote: In the cervical halfrings, the underlying bone band developed outgrowths connecting it with the underlying osteoderms, which simultaneously fused to each other

facts.statement: Caputegulae (skull armor plates) first ossified at the snout and rear rim before spreading to the middle regions of the skull.
facts.quote: On the skull, the caputegulae first ossified at the snout and the rear rim; gradually the ossification extended towards the middle regions

facts.statement: The mobile cricoid‑arytenoid joint and long arytenoid cartilages would have allowed easy opening of the glottis, enabling airflow control comparable to birds.
facts.quote: its mobile cricoid-arytenoid joint and long arytenoid cartilages would have enabled easy opening of the glottis, thus allowing air-flow control similar to that of birds

facts.statement: The laryngeal cartilages were ossified, showing that laryngeal ossification occurred in some non‑avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: the cartilages were ossified, implying that laryngeal ossification is a feature of some non-avian dinosaurs

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was likely capable of producing loud, possibly bird‑like vocalizations from a non‑laryngeal sound organ.
facts.quote: This structure suggests that Pinacosaurus was likely capable of making loud, possibly bird-like vocalizations and produced them from a non-laryngeal sound organ

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus lived in a semi‑desert environment with scattered oases, where only small theropods such as Velociraptor are known.
facts.quote: The habitat of Pinacosaurus consisted of a semi-desert interspersed with oases. No large theropods are known to have inhabited the ecosystem, though smaller ones like Velociraptor were present

facts.statement: Its relatively light build may have been an adaptation for agility to better confront small, fast theropods, with its tail club fast enough to strike them.
facts.quote: the relatively light build of Pinacosaurus was an adaptation to gain agility to better fight small theropods, the moderately large club being fast enough to hit these swift targets

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus lived in the Late Cretaceous, about 80 to 75 million years ago, during the Santonian to early Campanian in Asia.
facts.quote: vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 80 y 75 millones de años, a finales del Santoniense y principios del Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia

facts.statement: The skull of Pinacosaurus has two to five additional openings beside each nostril, whose function is still unknown.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus tiene entre dos y 5 orificios adicionales junto a las narinas, que todavía no han sido explicados

facts.statement: It possessed a thick tail club made of fused bones that served as a defensive weapon.
facts.quote: tenía una gruesa maza en el extremo final de su cola que utilizaba como arma defensiva

facts.statement: Strong tail muscles originating from the hips and legs allowed Pinacosaurus to lift and swing its heavy tail club side‑to‑side.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus necesitaban unos fuertes músculos en la cola para levantar la maza y blandirla de lado a lado, por lo que unos largos y poderosos músculos se extendían desde las caderas y las patas

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus differs from its distant relatives Gobisaurus and Shamosaurus by having extra openings in the nasal fossa and a forward‑pointing prefrontal caputegula.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus difiere de aquellos en posesión de aberturas adicionales en la fosa nasal y una caputegula puntiaguda que sobresale en el prefrontal, dirigida hacia el frente.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus lacks the ornamented posterior edge of the skull roof seen in Crichtonpelta and its cheek horn does not curve upward.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus se diferencia de Crichtonpelta en la falta de un borde posterior adornado del techo del cráneo y en que el cuerno de la mejilla no se curva hacia arriba.

facts.statement: P. grangeri possesses a notch in the snout armor just above the innermost nostril opening.
facts.quote: P. grangeri tiene una muesca en la armadura del hocico justo encima de la abertura de la nariz más interna.

facts.statement: P. mephistocephalus has scaly cheek horns that extend backward beyond the rear of the skull roof, with the horn tips marking the widest part of the skull.
facts.quote: P. mephistocephalus tiene cuernos escamosos que se extienden hacia atrás más allá de la parte posterior del techo del cráneo, y sus puntas representan el punto más ancho del cráneo

facts.statement: P. mephistocephalus shows a clear transverse narrowing of the skull roof at the level of the lacrimals, just in front of the eye sockets.
facts.quote: P. mephistocephalus también tiene un estrechamiento transversal claro del techo del cráneo al nivel de los lagrimales, justo en frente de las cuencas de los ojos.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. mephistocephalus has very long cheek horns, a trait also seen in a juvenile specimen (MPC 100/1344) assigned to P. grangeri.
facts.quote: El holotipo de P. mephistocephalus tiene cuernos muy largos en las mejillas, pero un espécimen juvenil, MPC 100/1344, que se encuentra como parte de u ngrupo de P. grangeri, muestra un alargamiento similar.

facts.statement: Known adult Pinacosaurus skulls are about 30 cm long.
facts.quote: Los cráneos adultos conocidos tienen una longitud de unos 30 centímetros.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus has exceptionally smooth premaxillae that formed a keratinous sheath over the snout in life.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus tiene premaxilares excepcionalmente lisos, los huesos frontales del hocico, que forman el núcleo óseo del pico superior, que en vida estaba cubierto con una hoja de cuerno.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Pinacosaurus bears roughly 14 teeth.
facts.quote: El maxilar tiene unos 14 dientes.

facts.statement: Each side of the Pinacosaurus nasal vestibule contains at least three smaller oval openings.
facts.quote: Con Pinacosaurus hay al menos tres por lado.

facts.statement: In Pinacosaurus the C opening lies beneath the A opening and the B opening is on the lower outer side of the vestibule.
facts.quote: en Pinacosaurus, el agujero C está debajo del agujero A y la abertura B está en el lado exterior inferior del vestíbulo.

facts.statement: Godefroit reported four pairs of nasal openings in 1999, and a juvenile described in 2003 showed five pairs.
facts.quote: Godefroit et al. describió 4 pares de aberturas en total en 1999, y en 2003 se describió un ejemplar juvenil con 5 pares de aberturas.

facts.statement: The known postcranial skeleton of Pinacosaurus is relatively lightweight, but most specimens are juveniles; the holotype of P. mephistocephalus is less than 3 m long.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la mayoría de estos representan juveniles, incluso el espécimen IMM 96BM3/1, el holotipo de P. mephistocephalus, no mide más de 3 metros.

facts.statement: Juvenile Pinacosaurus had four fused posterior dorsal vertebrae forming a sacral rod, three true sacral vertebrae, and a tail base of seven vertebrae with transverse processes.
facts.quote: Los juveniles tenían cuatro vértebras traseras de la espalda fusionadas en una "varilla sacra", tres verdaderos sacros y una base de la cola de siete vértebras que poseen procesos transversales.

facts.statement: Behind the tail base are about eight free vertebrae followed by roughly twenty stiffened vertebrae that form the handle of the tail club.
facts.quote: Detrás de estas se encuentran unas ocho vértebras "libres", seguidas de unas veinte vértebras endurecidas por proyecciones y que forman el "mango" del garrote de la cola.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus is the best-known ankylosaurid in Asia, represented by fifteen specimens including a nearly complete skeleton and several skulls.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus es el mejor anquilosáurido conocido en Asia con 15 especímenes, incluyendo un esqueleto casi completo, cinco cráneos algunos completos y otro parciales

facts.statement: The holotype of Pinacosaurus, specimen AMNH 6523, is a partially crushed skull with lower jaws and dermal plates discovered in 1923 by Walter Wallis Granger.
facts.quote: El holotipo, AMNH 6523, es un cráneo parcial aplastado, mandíbulas, y placas óseas dermales descubiertas en 1923 encontrados por Walter Wallis Granger.

facts.statement: The most complete skull of the genus belongs to a juvenile described by Teresa Maryańska in 1971 and 1977.
facts.quote: El mejor cráneo pertenece a un ejemplar joven descrito por Teresa Maryanska en 1971 y 1977.

facts.statement: Several groups of juvenile Pinacosaurus fossils were found together, indicating they died during a sandstorm.
facts.quote: dos descubrimientos de varios ejemplares jóvenes juntos, evidencia que murieron durante una tormenta de arena

facts.statement: Most juvenile Pinacosaurus skeletons are preserved lying on their backs with legs folded inward.
facts.quote: la mayoría de los juveniles de Pinacosaurus se encuentran boca abajo en una posición de reposo, con las piernas dobladas hacia adentro

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 that P. mephistocephalus is a junior synonym of P. grangeri.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul sugirió que P. mephistopheles era un sinónimo más moderno de P. grangeri

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum is classified within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, about 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Two fossil occurrences of Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum have been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was originally placed in Nodosauridae but is now considered a member of Ankylosauridae, likely within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Originalmente fue ubicado dentro de la familia Nodosauridae, pero hoy se lo considera perteneciente a Ankylosauridae y un miembro probable de Ankylosaurinae.

facts.statement: The habitat of Pinacosaurus consisted of a semi‑desert environment interspersed with oasis areas.
facts.quote: El hábitat de Pinacosaurus consistió en un semidesierto intercalado con oasis.

facts.statement: Juvenile Pinacosaurus individuals found together at Bayan Mandahu were all oriented the same way, suggesting they died as a traveling herd caught by a sandstorm.
facts.quote: En el grupo de juveniles que se encontraron juntos en Bayan Mandahu, los individuos estaban todos orientados en la misma dirección, lo que sugiere que representan una verdadera manada que viaja, matada y cubierta simultáneamente por una tormenta de arena.

facts.statement: During ontogeny, the ribs of juvenile Pinacosaurus initially fused to their vertebrae, and the forelimbs became considerably more robust while the hind limbs did not grow proportionally.
facts.quote: Durante su desarrollo ontogenético, en los juveniles al principio las costillas se fusionaron con sus vértebras. Las patas delanteras aumentaron considerablemente en robustez, mientras que las patas traseras no se hicieron más grandes en relación con el resto del esqueleto

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus likely relied heavily on muscular tongues and hyoid bones for feeding because its teeth were small and replaced slowly.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus y otros anquilosaurios probablemente dependían en gran medida de las lenguas musculares y los hiobranquios, huesos de la lengua, cuando se alimentaban, ya que sus dientes eran bastante pequeños y se reemplazaban a un ritmo relativamente lento.

facts.statement: A juvenile Pinacosaurus specimen preserves large paraglossal bones that show signs of muscular stress, a feature thought to be common among ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Un ejemplar juvenil de Pinacosaurus conserva grandes paraglosáceos, huesos triangulares o cartílagos ubicados en la lengua, que muestran signos de estrés muscular, y se cree que esta era una característica común de los anquilosaurios.
